note: Applies to EVERY category, not just one - checked against the item's properties block (not category_fields). See README.md.

base_value.note: Base economic / sale value in dollars ($). Mandatory on every item in the catalog.

weight_kg.note: Physical weight in kilograms (kg). Mandatory on every item in the catalog.

max_stack_size.note: Maximum inventory stack count (integer >= 1). Mandatory on every item in the catalog.

is_consumable.note: Whether the item is consumed / depleted upon use. Mandatory on every item in the catalog.

is_spawnable.note: Whether this asset is placed into the world during terrain generation. When true, the asset must also declare a 'spawning' block naming at least one target biome (spawning.biomes[]). When false or absent, the asset exists only as an inventory/crafting item and is never scattered by the generator. Defaults to false when omitted, so older manifests stay valid.

thirst_restore.note: score, same -100/+100 scale as the other player stats. Drinkable water containers and watery food/drink items only (positive). 0 for everything else.

energy_restore.note: score, same -100/+100 scale as the other player stats. Beds (full rest) and seating (couches/chairs, a lesser rest) only (positive). 0 for everything else.

stamina_restore.note: score, same -100/+100 scale as the other player stats - a shorter-term exertion resource, distinct from energy_restore's longer-term tiredness/sleep. Mainly food (quick energy from eating). 0 for everything else.

wellness_modifier.note: Wellness is the player's overall health/sickness meter, and it's broader than just consumption. Sources of wellness change, most of which are RUNTIME EVENTS/CONDITIONS rather than a static per-item value (so most items stay 0 here even though they're relevant to the mechanic): (1) consumption - contaminated/unfiltered water and questionable food lower it, clean filtered water and wholesome food raise it (this is what the field captures on food/water items); (2) injury - physical harm while doing risky work (e.g. handling an aggressive animal, see ranching.temperament) is a runtime event, not an item property; (3) environmental exposure - working in/near unclean conditions (manure piles, see waste category) lowers it via proximity, similar to happiness_modifier's proximity model; (4) sleep deprivation - insufficient energy_restore over time is a runtime accumulation, not a single item's value; (5) hygiene - NOT SHOWERING lowers wellness over time; there is currently NO shower/bathing item in the catalog to raise it back - this is a real gap, see the queued asset request; (6) WEATHER EXPOSURE - being out in hot sun without drinking (thirst_restore not being met) lowers wellness on top of the thirst penalty itself; being outside in cold/winter weather without adequate winter gear also lowers wellness. There is currently NO clothing/apparel category or winter gear item in the catalog at all - a real gap, see the queued Winter Coat asset request; once winter gear exists it should carry a positive wellness_modifier (or a dedicated cold-resistance field) representing protection from this penalty. DESIGN RULE: wellness can ONLY be raised by the player deliberately taking care of themselves (eating well, hydrating, sleeping, showering, avoiding injury/unclean exposure) - it must never passively regenerate on its own or rise from unrelated sources. RUNTIME REQUIREMENT: wellness itself should feed back into OTHER stats, not just be a dead-end meter - low wellness should reduce max stamina and reduce happiness. This cross-stat relationship is game logic, not a catalog field.

placeable.label: Placeable
placeable.note: Whether the player can put this item on the ground. Opt in: true for crates, structures, utilities and other things that stand in the world; default false (tools, food and materials in hand do nothing). The first left click brings out a shadow preview, R rotates it, Enter or a second click places it. Seeds that plant a growth group are never placed.

stores.label: Sold At
stores.note: The phone shops that sell this item (depot, lumber, grocer, feed, water, vehicles, equipment, livestock, furniture, voltvision, trailershack). The manifest is the ONLY place this lives: the phone builds each shop from the catalog. Setting it makes the item buyable at base_value (is_buyable true).

sale_unit.label: Sale Unit
sale_unit.note: How a shop counts it: ea, kit, box, bale, packet, tank ... (default ea).

store_category.label: Shop Label
store_category.note: The chip label a shop shows for it when it differs from its asset category default (for example Trailer Parts).

store_overrides.label: Per-Shop Overrides
store_overrides.note: One shop that sells it differently: {"trailershack": {"category": "Trailer Repair", "unit": "ea", "price": 35}}. Edited in the manifest JSON.

support_surface.label: Carries Things (pallet)
support_surface.note: A placed one carries items on top (a pallet): things placed over its deck rest on it, packed side by side and stacked up to their stacking limit. A pallet that still carries things cannot be picked up. Needs placeable = true.

attach_surface.label: Mounts On
attach_surface.note: An item that mounts on a FINISHED building instead of standing on the ground: wall (a breaker box, a wall sconce, a switch) or ceiling (a ceiling light). With the item in hand a left click brings out a preview over the walls / ceiling, a second click or Enter mounts it, a right click takes it down. Leave empty for everything else. Such an item is not placeable (placeable false). See docs/ATTACHED_ITEMS.md. Model: the back of a wall item is the plane y = 0 sticking out towards -y; a ceiling item hangs from its top.

attach_side.label: Mount Side
attach_side.note: For a wall mount: which side of the wall it goes on. interior = inside a room (switches, sconces), exterior = outside the building (a breaker box, a wall lantern), either = both.

provides_power.label: Brings Power
provides_power.note: Mounted on the OUTSIDE of a building it brings electricity to that building (the outdoor breaker box). Lights whose manifest entry says requires_power stay dark in a building without it.

look_target.label: Building Look: Parts
look_target.note: Used as a construction material, this item decides how parts of the building LOOK. One or more of: roof, walls (logs, siding), interior (paint), floor (carpet, tile, flooring), chimney (brick, stone), foundation (see Foundation Style), separated by commas (bricks: "chimney,foundation"). Leave empty for items that do not.

look_color.label: Building Look: Colour
look_color.note: The colour of that part of the building as #RRGGBB (birch logs white-cream, pine warm brown, shingles slate grey).

look_metallic.label: Building Look: Metallic
look_metallic.note: 0 = not metal, 1 = bare metal (a tin roof, steel siding).

look_style.label: Building Look: Foundation Style
look_style.note: For an item whose parts include foundation: the foundation style it builds: poured (the slab), block (concrete block stem wall), brick (brick or stone stem wall, coloured by Look Colour) or stilts (piles under a deck).

burn_minutes.label: Burns For (game minutes)
burn_minutes.note: Fuel for a fireplace: placed in a fireplace (right click the chimney of a finished building with it) it burns for this many game minutes. 0 = not a fireplace fuel.

lights_fires.label: Lights Fires
lights_fires.note: A lighter or match: right click a fireplace that has fuel in it with this item in hand to light the fire. It is not used up.

fence_style.label: Fence Style
fence_style.note: A fence material the player builds with: wood (post and rail) or wire. With it in hand each click places a post; the panels fill in between the posts when the fence is built.

fence_panel_m.label: Fence Panel Length (m)
fence_panel_m.note: How far one panel of this fencing reaches between two posts; a run of L metres uses ceil(L / this) panels.

fence_height_m.label: Fence Height (m)
fence_height_m.note: How tall the finished fence stands.

fence_post_item.label: Fence Post Item
fence_post_item.note: The item id of the post this fencing is built on (one per post, taken from the hotbar when the fence is built).

gate_width_m.label: Gate Width (m)
gate_width_m.note: A gate: with it in hand, a click on a built fence takes the fence out for this width and stands the gate in the gap. Empty = not a gate.

gate_style.label: Gate Style
gate_style.note: How the gate looks: wood or metal.

path_kind.label: Path / Road Kind
path_kind.note: A surface the player lays as a smooth curved route (PathBuilder): path (narrow, for walking) or road (wide, for vehicles). Empty = not a path material.

path_width_m.label: Path Width (m)
path_width_m.note: How wide the laid surface is (paths about 1.2 m, roads about 4 m).

path_style.label: Path Surface
path_style.note: How the surface looks. Asphalt also gets a centre lane marking.

path_m_per_item.label: Metres Per Item
path_m_per_item.note: How many metres of route one item lays; a route of L metres uses ceil(L / this) items.

is_blueprint.label: Blueprint
is_blueprint.note: Bought once, starts a build when held (structure site, path or road route) and is never used up. Shown on the blueprint blue (#35637C). Structures that build in stages are blueprints automatically.

path_material_item.label: Path Material Item
path_material_item.note: On a path or road blueprint: the item id of the material it lays (one per path_m_per_item metres), taken from the hotbar or the work site.
